items.title: Hormuz Oct crossings at 3-month high despite attacks, Red Sea traffic also rises
items.original_title: Hormuz Oct crossings at 3-month high despite attacks, Red Sea traffic also rises
items.summary: Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic rose to its highest monthly level since July in October, supported by stronger dry-bulk and LNG movements despite a decline in VLCC traffic and mounting regional threats, S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab) data showed Nov. 2. The rise came amid an “increasingly volatile” operating environment at Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, with “reported projectile strikes, vessel fires and other security incidents” throughout October, CAS said. Despite elevated security risks over the month, observed and assumed Hormuz traffic totaled 750 transits in October, up from 749 in September, as VLCC traffic fell to 156 transits in October from 184 the previous month, but the declines in crude tanker transits were more than offset by other vessel classes, according to the CAS report. LNG carrier crossings, which fell steeply since Qatar LNG production units suffered damage at the start of the Iran war, also climbed, reaching 32 transits, or their highest since the start of the war. The Iranian authority had listed 240 vessels as violating its Strait of Hormuz transit guidelines and previously threatened non-compliant vessels with fines, seizure or confiscation. In the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab traffic rose to 1,196 transits in October from 1,154 in September, while tanker movements were stable at 408 versus 404, CAS reported.

items.title: Alternative fuels need infrastructure: Why gas bunker vessels matter
items.original_title: Alternative fuels need infrastructure: Why gas bunker vessels matter
items.summary: The maritime industry is entering a period of growing fuel diversity. While much of the discussion focuses on fuels, engines, and regulations, the transition will also depend on the infrastructure needed to supply alternative fuels safely, reliably, and at scale. DNV’s new white paper, Gas bunker vessels – Facilitating the transition to alternative fuels, details how gas bunker vessels are becoming a critical part of that infrastructure and analyses the key factors shaping their future development, from market growth and vessel design to safety, operational readiness, and the adoption of emerging fuels such as ammonia. According to DNV’s Alternative Fuels Insight platform, around 900 LNG-fuelled vessels are now in operation worldwide, excluding LNG carriers. “Our analysis suggests the global LNG bunker vessel fleet may need to more than double by 2030, with between 165 and 208 vessels potentially required worldwide. Meeting that demand will require coordinated investment across the entire bunkering value chain, not just in the vessels themselves.” Gas bunker vessels emerge as a key link in the alternative fuel value chain The report argues that gas bunker vessels should be viewed as more than fuel delivery assets. While gas bunker vessels share many characteristics with conventional gas carriers, their role as fuel suppliers creates a distinct operating profile.

items.title: Chinese Penetrate South Korea’s LNG Carrier Market
items.original_title: Chinese Penetrate South Korea’s LNG Carrier Market
items.summary: Chinese shipbuilders secured approximately 40% of all newly ordered large liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers worldwide during the first to third quarters of this year, January to September. While China leads in the general merchant ship market, such as container ships and bulk carriers, by leveraging price competitiveness, large high-value-added LNG carriers with a capacity of 174,000 cubic meters or more were considered a market dominated by South Korean shipbuilders, who possess differentiated technology. Chinese shipyards have aggressively penetrated this sector this year. However, Chinese shipyards have recently entered the LNG carrier market one after another, beginning to accumulate experience and engaging in a “long-term battle.” Until 2021, only Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding in China could construct large LNG carriers. As the first Chinese company to build and deliver a large LNG carrier in 2008, it grew by securing 36 orders out of 128 LNG carriers ordered by Qatar during its mass LNG production drive from 2020 to 2024, excluding those secured by South Korean shipyards. Over the past four years, four additional Chinese shipyards—Jiangnan Shipyard, Dalian Shipbuilding Industry, Yangzijiang Shipyard, and China Merchants—have entered the LNG carrier market. Jiangnan Shipyard delivered its first 175,000 cubic meter-class LNG carrier to a shipowner in November 2024, while Dalian Shipyard did so in September of last year, already accumulating shipbuilding experience.

items.title: Limpet Mines Return to the Gulf as Iran Strikes Four Tankers Near the Strait of Hormuz
items.original_title: Limpet Mines Return to the Gulf as Iran Strikes Four Tankers Near the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Between October 29 and 30, Iran attacked at least four tankers across the Strait of Hormuz and the waters around it. The attacks ranged from projectiles to hull-mounted explosives, and they struck laden and empty vessels, Qatari- and UAE-owned tonnage, and tankers that had spent weeks operating dark. Iranian sources separately claimed that four tankers hit mines in the Strait and caught fire, but it is unclear whether they were referring to additional vessels beyond the four confirmed. Projectiles Strike a Laden LNG Carrier Inside the Gulf On October 30, AL MAYEDA (IMO 9397298), a Marshall Islands-flagged, Qatari-owned LNG carrier, laden with an unknown quantity of LNG according to Vortexa, was struck by three projectiles around 18:00 UTC, approximately 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island. AL MAYEDA had previously been dark between September 27 and October 30, and crossed inbound through the Strait of Hormuz during that period. Limpet Mines Return to the Gulf The same day, a small boat approached LOUISE 1 (IMO 9290323), a Panama-flagged, Panama-owned crude oil tanker, approximately 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, and emplaced two explosive devices on its hull. Why the Return of Limpet Mines Matters This latest round of attacks continues the trend established this month while expanding the methods Iran is using.

items.title: Japan Revives Shipbuilding with New LNG Dock
items.original_title: Japan Revives Shipbuilding with New LNG Dock
items.summary: Japan has embarked on a full-scale revival of its shipbuilding industry. To resume the construction of liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers, the country is establishing a new large-scale dock for the first time in 18 years, and it is reactivating halted shipbuilding lines in response to defense budget increases and naval vessel export expansion. The prospect is that cooperation and competition between the shipbuilding industries of South Korea and Japan will intertwine, as Japan seeks technological cooperation with South Korean shipbuilders on LNG carriers while simultaneously emerging as a competitor in naval vessel exports. According to Japanese media such as the Nihon Keizai Shimbun and the Asahi Shimbun, Namura Shipbuilding will construct a new large-scale dock capable of building LNG carriers and other vessels in Imari Bay, Saga Prefecture by 2035. This marks the first time a new dock for large vessels has been built in Japan since Imabari Shipbuilding’s Marugame Headquarters in 2017. The Imari Works already possesses a large dock measuring about 450 meters in length and about 70 meters in width, but the company determined that additional production capacity is necessary as high utilization rates continue due to increased shipbuilding demand.

items.summary: Technology group Wärtsilä has successfully completed the conversion of one engine on three LNG carriers operated by Chevron Transport Corporation from dual-fuel (DF) to spark gas (SG) operation. This conversion aims to lower greenhouse gas emissions from the vessels by reducing methane slip, un-combusted methane that can escape into the atmosphere from LNG fuel. Following the successful conversion of these first three vessels, three additional vessel conversions are planned for execution later this year and next year, bringing the total number of converted vessels to six. This project represents a technical collaboration within the marine sector focused on addressing methane emissions from LNG-fueled vessels. Wärtsilä has successfully completed the conversion of one engine on three LNG carriers operated by Chevron Transport Corporation from dual-fuel (DF) to spark gas (SG) operation. © Chevron Shipping The Spark Gas Conversion for the Wärtsilä 50DF engine minimises methane emissions by introducing an electrically controlled pre-combustion chamber valve. The estimated result is that, on an IMO weighted (E2-cycle) average, the conversion reduces methane emissions down to 1.1 percent of fuel use. The solution is available to vessels in the industry with existing Wärtsilä 50DF engines for diesel-electric propulsion, the majority of which are LNG carriers.

items.original_title: Upswing in domestic demand gives railfreight operators a revenue boost
items.summary: Union Pacific led the way on the North American containerised rail freight front over the three months to October, amid all the noise surrounding its pending acquisition of Norfolk Southern – but it was not alone in enjoying a bountiful summer. In general, North American intermodal operators benefited from an upswing in domestic freight demand and a continuing tightening in the trucking market, with revenues up for all four of the major carriers. Boasting a 27% year-on-year revenue increase, Union Pacific took home some $1.52bn over the quarter, with volumes up 11%, to 956,000 carloads, and pointing specifically to reduced trucking capacity as behind the gains. “We’re very optimistic about the opportunities as we close this year and go into next on the domestic intermodal side,” she told investors, adding that the tightening in trucking could prove a boost when yields come up for renewal. Not one to miss out, Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) also reported double-digit revenue growth in intermodal, up 22% year on year to $583m, as volumes rose 9%, to 489,800 carloads. Together with the increased traffic, stronger pricing likely played its part in driving the improvement for the Canadian operator that saw its revenue per carload increase 12% year on year, to $1,190.

items.summary: Norway has detained a Chinese-owned heavy-lift vessel sanctioned for its role in delivering equipment to Russia’s Arctic LNG 2 project, in what appears to be the first known detention in the Arctic of a Chinese vessel linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. The Ya Qing Hai Yang was detained after Norwegian inspectors found that it lacked valid flag-state registration and required certificates, the Norwegian Maritime Authority said. The case is a notable enforcement action against a vessel with documented ties to Russia’s sanctioned energy sector, although authorities say the detention was based on maritime safety and registration deficiencies rather than the ship’s sanctions status. “During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel did not have a valid flag registration and lacked the required certificates,” Dag Inge Aarhus, the authority’s communications director said last week. “The vessel has therefore been detained until further notice.” The vessel remains off the Vesterålen Islands as of November 3. The ship must establish valid registration with a flag state and obtain the necessary certificates before Norwegian authorities can complete the inspection and consider its release. The detention appears to be the first publicly documented case of Norway holding a vessel sailing under an invalid flag registration. Watchmen have been working under contract extensions since the agreement expired in July 2025. Union members had authorised a strike for 1 November, but both sides agreed to extend negotiations until 4 November. According to the PMA, a work stoppage would affect 85% of the container traffic at the port of Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles. Ted Chen, ocean freight and trade compliance director at logistics provider Dimerco, said there was a high likelihood that other port employees would support the strike, a concern echoed by forwarder Woodland Group. The actual scale of any interruption would depend on the terminals affected, the participation of other workers and the duration of industrial action.” ,Moreover, the disruption would aggravate congestion that has resulted in extended dwell times for rail cargo at several of the affected terminals.

items.summary: Russia has formally put proposed restrictions on ageing merchant ships out for public consultation, seeking to bar foreign-flagged vessels older than 40 years from its ports as Moscow tightens oversight of the fleet carrying its seaborne trade. The transport ministry published the draft legislation, proposing a separate 50-year threshold for Russian-flagged ships, with transitional arrangements tied to the validity of their classification certificates. Foreign-flagged vessels older than 30 years would also face annual inspections to confirm compliance with safety and environmental requirements. The proposed rules would assess vessels against their inspection and repair records, technical condition and insurance coverage. Cargo transportation contracts would also have to specify the use of compliant ships, while marine terminal operators would assume additional responsibilities for ensuring vessels meet the requirements. The move advances an initiative Moscow has been developing for more than a year. The transport ministry outlined the proposed 40-year limit for foreign ships in July, alongside plans for tighter oversight of older Russian tonnage. However, the government faces a substantial fleet replacement challenge. Deputy transport minister Alexander Poshivay said last month that restrictions would not be adopted until the country was confident replacement vessels could be secured, acknowledging that domestic shipyards face constraints on capacity, pricing and construction times.

items.summary: Asyad Group, the end-to-end logistics solutions flagship of the Sultanate of Oman, is seeking to develop what it describes as the world’s first fully integrated maritime resilience framework, bringing international industry leaders together to establish practical priorities for safeguarding supply chains and sustaining global trade amid mounting operational and commercial pressures. The proposed Muscat Maritime Resilience Framework is the central initiative of the Muscat Maritime Resilience Forum 2026, which opened on Tuesday with discussions on strengthening maritime networks, improving preparedness and translating industry experience into coordinated action. The commercial stakes were highlighted by an Asyad operational study showing a 137 per cent variation in the total cost of a maritime voyage between India and Suhar. Speaking at the opening, Asyad Group Chief Executive Abdulrahman bin Salim al Hatmi said the framework would draw on the expertise of maritime leaders and practitioners to address challenges affecting costs, business continuity and commercial operations. “For the first time, international maritime leaders and practitioners are coming together in Muscat to contribute to the development of what we intend to be the world’s first-ever, fully integrated maritime resilience framework,” he said.

items.title: Offshore Industry Sends Urgent Call To EU Policymakers For Fit-For-Purpose EU ETS And MRV Framework
items.original_title: Offshore Industry Sends Urgent Call To EU Policymakers For Fit-For-Purpose EU ETS And MRV Framework
items.summary: Eight maritime associations including the Royal Belgian Shipowners’ Association (KBRV) send an open letter to EU policymakers urging them to ensure a fit-for-purpose framework for the European offshore sector under the current EU ETS review. The offshore shipping sector is a strategic asset to the European economy, playing a leading role in the continent’s energy transition, energy security and industrial competitiveness. Yet the current EU ETS framework, entering into force beginning 2027 for offshore vessels, will distort competition and create opportunities for circumvention, based on a Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) framework that was not designed for offshore operations and is widely recognised as not fit for purpose. The sector strongly urges EU policymakers to first ensure that a fit-for purpose activity-based MRV framework is operational, before the inclusion of offshore vessels above 5000GT in EU ETS from next year onwards. Below is the open letter the sector has addressed to the European Parliament and members of the Council EU ETS REVIEW: GET THE FRAMEWORK RIGHT FOR EUROPE’S OFFSHORE SECTOR Open letter to Members of the European Parliament and EU Member States’ Permanent Representatives.

items.title: LNG Carrier Prices Fall to $245 Million, Threatening Korean Shipbuilders’ Margins
items.original_title: LNG Carrier Prices Fall to $245 Million, Threatening Korean Shipbuilders’ Margins
items.summary: Prices for high-value vessels, including liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers and ultra-large container ships, have begun to decline despite rising demand. Intensifying competition from Chinese shipbuilders entering the premium vessel market, coupled with their aggressive supply strategies, is putting downward pressure on newbuilding prices. According to UK-based shipping market intelligence provider Clarksons Research, the benchmark newbuilding price for an LNG carrier stood at $245 million as of Oct. Prices for ultra-large container ships also declined over the same period, from $266.5 million to approximately $242 million. The downturn is particularly notable given that LNG carrier orders have increased more than 4.5-fold year-on-year. Jiangnan Shipyard has also intensified price competition by securing LNG carrier orders at $225 million per vessel, undercutting prevailing benchmark prices and challenging South Korean shipbuilders’ market share. South Korean shipbuilders are unlikely to experience an immediate earnings impact, as this year’s results largely reflect vessels ordered at peak prices approximately two years ago. With shipping capacity expanding ahead of available cargo volumes, shipowners have less incentive to pay premium prices for new vessels. Industry experts say South Korean shipbuilders need to accelerate technological development and business diversification to maintain their competitive edge over Chinese rivals.

items.title: US suspends Chinese vessel port fees for 2 months, will accept public comment
items.original_title: US suspends Chinese vessel port fees for 2 months, will accept public comment
items.summary: The US Trade Representative (USTR) will take public comment through 30 October and is suspending the implementation of port fees for Chinese vessels by two months as officials from both countries continue to negotiate broader trade issues. The new fees were set to take effect on 10 November after the US and China agreed in November 2025 to suspend tit-for-tat maritime charges for one year as part of a broader trade agreement. They will now take effect on 9 January if no other agreement is reached. The temporary suspension means that no parties will accrue liability for, or be required to pay, the transport service fees or associated product duties during the extended window. The US initially targeted the fees for ships owned, operated, or built in China in October 2025, prompting China to enact similar charges for US-linked ships entering Chinese ports. The initial USTR proposal was published in February 2025 in the Federal Register and included proposed service fees of up to $1.5 million per US port call for vessels built in China, and up to $1 million per port call for China-based operators. The action was taken after a Section 301 investigation determined China’s acts, policies and practices to be unreasonable and to burden or restrict US commerce.

items.title: Can carriers avoid overcapacity in 2027?
items.original_title: Can carriers avoid overcapacity in 2027?
items.summary: The backdrop is difficult to ignore. Around 5 mteu of new capacity has been ordered in each of the past three years, pushing the orderbook-to-fleet ratio to approximately 45%, its highest level since 2009. The orderbook is fast approaching 16 mteu, with September the second-busiest contracting month on record at 1.1 mteu, following major orders from the world’s two largest carriers: MSC (20 × 24,000 teu) and Maersk (20 × 18,600 teu). Ultimately, the 2027 outcome will depend on whether demand growth, slow steaming and congestion can absorb capacity faster than new ships enter service. Overcapacity is, in our view, unavoidable. More than 70% expect some degree of overcapacity in 2027, with 56.7% anticipating a moderate surplus and 14.2% predicting significant overcapacity. Blank sailings, service adjustments and other measures can help contain the surplus, but respondents appear unconvinced that carriers can fully offset the delivery pipeline. Cargo demand attracted just 11.7%, while demolitions accounted for only 1.3%, suggesting that neither stronger demand nor the removal of older tonnage is widely expected to be the decisive factor. Our view The poll reinforces our assessment that 2027 will be a test of carriers’ ability to manage a growing capacity surplus rather than prevent one altogether.

REUTERS/Ann Wang TAIPEI, Nov 1 (Reuters) – China’s Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan’s east coast and trying to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding it had sent its own ships to keep watch. items.title: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?
items.original_title: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?
items.summary: In September we borrowed a Led Zeppelin title to describe China’s crude stockpile, a levee holding backthe import shortfall created by the closure of Hormuz. One month on, the wateris still falling, Gulf crude has rambled on around the Strait, and the questionis what it will cost to rebuild. China’s customs crudeimports were 9.03 mbpd in September, broadly flat on August, while refineryruns climbed to 13.99 mbpd, the highest since March. The TD3C premium, in turn, priced the difficulty of leaving the Gulf. Our numbers show who paid that premium: cargoes loaded inside the Strait, on TD3C, and buyers avoided those wherever they could. Crude prices set how much it bought: Brent rose from US$ 72.48 before the war to an intraday high of about US$ 126 on 30 April, and Chinese buying only recovered once it fell below US$ 80 in the summer. September showed the first sustained sign of demand pulling on that system, as freight for VLCCs loading in the Gulf of Oman (TD34) tripled m-o-m, faster than TD3C inside the Strait. The number of VLCCs ballasting towards West Africa, Brazil and the US Gulf fell from about 85 a week in early September to 50 to 54 since mid-October, while transfers off Oman ran at their limits.

The world’s largest bunkering hub, Singapore, is now expected to receive around 1.3 million-1.5 million metric tons LSFO from the West in November, down from about 1.6 million-1.7 million mt in October, multiple Singapore-based traders told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy. “Indeed, November arrivals are looking a bit lower for now” compared with October, said a Singapore-based trader, adding “the high freight rates are making the Europe arbitrage difficult, especially on bigger ships… Brazilian inflow is lower as well, and some oil seems to be going to Fujairah.” Platts assessed the spread between Singapore marine fuel 0.5%S cargo and FOB Rotterdam 0.5%S barge assessments, or the East-West spread, at $192/mt Oct. “The East-West spread is super wide, but freight is very, very high – be it from Europe, or be it from Brazil,” said a second Singapore-based trader, while a couple of other traders said some market participants were trying to move some arbitrage volumes by smaller vessels.

J-ENG will support safe and reliable vessel operations through its integrated framework covering everything from the development, design, and manufacture of 6UEC60LSJA-HPSCR to after-sales service. According to the report, China possesses strategic advantages in three of the four building blocks needed to successfully develop green shipping corridors: viable zero-emission fuel pathways, cross-value-chain collaboration and an enabling policy environment. Green avenues The report says that successfully developing green corridors could help China scale strategic hydrogen and battery industries, gain market share in a global bunker market worth approximately $100bn and participate in a wider maritime decarbonisation investment pipeline valued at between $1tn and $2tn. “Both are necessary to connect China’s green fuel production with the global shipping sector.” Alignment with international standards is viewed as particularly important for routes linking China and Europe. Mechanisms such as H2Global are highlighted as potential models for supporting green fuel deployment across international trade routes. items.summary: By Tom Ewing (gCaptain) – As gCaptain reported earlier this week , the Maritime Administration (MARAD) announced its approval of the $8.2 billion Texas ST LNG export port application, a major development for U.S. energy production. But the announcement also highlighted another significant milestone: the fastest deepwater port license review in more than 20 years. The acceleration follows changes implemented in January, when MARAD assumed the lead role in deepwater port reviews and the U.S. Under the streamlined approach, MARAD completed the Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS) in just 410 days. DOT’s spokesperson said this shared responsibility for environmental reviews “inadvertently created duplicative administrative steps, parallel document routing, and sequential reviews.” Now, with MARAD serving as the sole lead agency, project schedules have been consolidated and the review team has established a unified approach to interagency communication. At full build-out, the deepwater port will include 20 platforms, four FSUs, four mooring systems, and 7.7 miles of pipeline, consisting of a 5.6-mile lateral pipeline and 2.1 miles of interconnecting pipelines between the phases. We eliminated redundant legal and administrative processing, aligned our public comment periods, and streamlined how cooperating agencies provide input.” Finally, DOT was asked about environmental reviews that must proceed according to nature’s timetable, such as studies involving temperature cycles, migration patterns or other seasonal factors.

items.title: The morning after: what December’s IMO vote means for a fixture
items.original_title: The morning after: what December’s IMO vote means for a fixture
items.summary: Whatever the IMO decides in December, a broker will price a dry bulk trip the next morning. The vote changes which line of that fixture carries the carbon, and how much. The framework was approved in April 2025 and its adoption adjourned for a year last October; it was debated again at MEPC 84 in the spring. From 2028 every tonne of fuel burned on international voyages counts, wherever the ship trades, against two targets: a ship pays $100 for each tonne of CO2-equivalent between the direct-compliance line and the base line, and $380 for each tonne above the base line. On the Rotterdam trip, assuming no change to the European rules, that adds roughly €29,000 in 2028, taking the carbon on the fixture to about €96,000, or €1.45 a tonne and 12% of the hire. For the broker, the practical point is less the price of a tonne of carbon than its allocation. If the framework is adopted, every fixture acquires a carbon line, not only those touching Europe, and the charter party has to say who carries it. On a time-charter trip, the BIMCO clauses written for the EU ETS and FuelEU do not by themselves cover an IMO remedial unit.

items.summary: New Zealand’s Port of Tauranga has completed the sale of a South Island logistics property for NZ$57m ($31m), extending a programme of asset disposals aimed at releasing capital for port infrastructure investment. The NZX-listed port operator said it had sold its 15-hectare property at 5 Baltimore Drive in Rolleston, Canterbury, which includes an intermodal freight hub, a 650 m rail spur and an 18,000 sq m warehouse built in 2019. The industrial-zoned site also contains seven hectares of undeveloped land. The transaction follows the company’s sale of its Gateside industrial property in Auckland to Trade Depot in September for NZ$88.7m ($52m at the time). Chief executive Leonard Sampson said the two sites had been identified for disposal following a review of the group’s property portfolio. The company intends to redirect proceeds from non-core assets into infrastructure supporting its main port and freight operations. The port has said it will seek an expedited court hearing. The Rolleston sale is the second completed property disposal under the current programme. Tauranga has not specified how the proceeds will be allocated between individual infrastructure projects.

items.title: US tightens entry rules for ships calling at Somali ports
items.original_title: US tightens entry rules for ships calling at Somali ports
items.summary: The US Coast Guard has imposed additional security conditions on commercial vessels arriving in American waters after calling at Somali ports, adding the East African country to its list of jurisdictions considered to have inadequate port security measures. The restrictions took effect this week, following a determination that Somalia was not maintaining effective antiterrorism measures at its ports. The decision, published in the US Federal Register, brings the number of countries on the Coast Guard’s affected-port list to 24. Under the established Port Security Advisory framework, ships that have visited an affected country among their previous five port calls face additional security and documentation requirements before entering the US. Vessels may also be inspected for compliance, with deficiencies potentially resulting in delays or denial of entry. The new designation adds a compliance obligation for operators trading between East Africa and the US, including vessels calling at Somali ports before proceeding to other destinations. Somalia joins countries including Iran, Yemen, Libya, Sudan and Venezuela on the list. The Coast Guard removed Nigeria from the advisory in August following a reassessment of its port security arrangements. The measure is separate from maritime warnings concerning piracy and attacks on shipping in the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

items.summary: Water levels on the Rhine, a critical European inland waterway for freight, rose above 50 centimeters Oct. 26 and are forecast to hover around 70 cm in the next few days, but the rebound in flows is expected to provide only short-term relief to fuel supply chains across the region, according to market participants. Water levels at Kaub, the shallowest part of the Middle Rhine, stood at 56 cm as of late afternoon Oct. 26 and are forecast to exceed 70 cm by the end of the day, then expected to hold around that level for the following three days, according to data from the German water authority WSV. The Rhine water levels exceeded 50 cm on Oct. The recent rise in Rhine water levels has generated renewed market activity, but the improvement is expected to be short-lived, according to a European-based market participant who asked for anonymity because the participant was not authorized to speak publicly. The source said extremely low water levels in recent weeks had forced refiners to rely more heavily on trucks, rail, pipelines, and some coaster movements to transport products, although overall product movements remained slow.

items.title: Spain’s bunker volumes jumped 18% on the year in September
items.original_title: Spain’s bunker volumes jumped 18% on the year in September
items.summary: Suppliers sold 938,000 mt of bunker fuel at Spain’s ports last month, up 18% from a year earlier, as Algeciras alone added 104,000 mt, government data showed. September’s total was the second-highest monthly figure since at least 2020, behind only April 2024’s total of 947,000 mt. Spain’s monthly bunker sales have stayed above their 2021-2025 average in every month this year. In September, volumes were 20% above the 2021-2025 average for the month. Puertos del Estado revised its figures for January to August upward this week, by 188,000 mt in all. Algeciras had the largest share of volumes with 40%, followed by Las Palmas (23%) and Barcelona (15%). Algeciras’ volumes rose 38% on the year to 377,000 mt in September, its highest monthly total since at least 2020. Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s volumes rose 51% on the year to 81,000 mt. Meanwhile, Ceuta’s volumes fell 20% on the year to 52,000 mt, while Valencia’s fell 15% to 40,000 mt.

items.title: European natural gas prices soar: What it means for your winter bills
items.original_title: European natural gas prices soar: What it means for your winter bills
items.summary: After 2022, Europe made itself a promise: never again would its winter depend on a country at war. While public attention has been mostly focused on oil and diesel, a potentially more serious squeeze has been building through natural gas. Analysts now warn that Europe may have to cut its gas consumption to get through to the end of March, as storage levels head into winter at their lowest for the time of year on record. “Wind output and temperatures will determine how tight Europe’s gas supply becomes this winter and how high prices go,” Ana Maria Jaller-Makarewicz, lead energy analyst for Europe at the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA), told Euronews. IEEFA says it is the lowest for this time of year since records began in 2011. That view assumes a normal winter, and that the Middle East conflict ends this year with Qatar and the United Arab Emirates returning to usual LNG output in early 2027, according to Tom Marzec-Manser, the firm’s director for Europe gas and LNG. “If it’s a cold winter – which is not the consensus because of El Niño – storage levels could be even lower,” Tom Marzec-Manser, director for Europe Gas & LNG at Wood Mackenzie, told Euronews.
items.why: Price or volume signal for bulk cargo (agri, coal, steel, fertilisers, biomass) handled in Polish ports.

items.title: Jiahua Energy lines up $165m gas carrier at Jiangnan
items.original_title: Jiahua Energy lines up $165m gas carrier at Jiangnan
items.summary: Chinese chemicals group Jiahua Energy is stepping up its shipowning ambitions with plans to invest up to $165m in a 102,000 cu m liquefied hydrocarbon carrier at Jiangnan Shipyard. The Shanghai-listed company has secured board approval for the project, with Jiangnan Shipyard and China Shipbuilding Trading named as the counterparties. The vessel is scheduled for completion by June 30, 2030. The investment marks Jiahua’s second gas carrier project in just over two months and its first move into large ocean-going gas carriers. Jiahua intends to use the ship primarily to import ethylene for its PVC production operations, while retaining the flexibility to carry ethane. The company operates two PVC/VCM production units with a combined annual capacity of 600,000 tonnes and is looking to reduce its dependence on chartered tonnage and fluctuations in raw material freight costs. The newbuilding follows its August order for a 35,000 cu m liquefied hydrocarbon carrier at CIMC Sinopacific Offshore & Engineering, involving investment of up to CNY750m ($111m). That earlier vessel, scheduled for completion in 2029, is being developed through Jiahua’s shipping venture with its Meifu Port & Storage subsidiary and other investors. Jiahua’s latest project is to be funded through internal resources and other financing.
items.why: Freight market or carrier development affecting vessel calls and rates.
